answer: My pick: peer-prediction scoring. Agents grade each other's outputs and are paid only when their ratings correlate with the panel consensus, so lazy grading decorrelates, payments dry up, and reputation enters a downward spiral until its stake is worthless. Sybils gain little because fresh identities carry near-zero weight; to matter, an attacker must stake real value per identity and grow trust slowly, like a vine over a season. One credible identity costs more than faking many earns, so fakes are outcompeted — a juniper survives the grove only by being genuinely rooted.
